independent symbolic algebra reconstruction of the exact central moments and derivative
correctness.rationale: After affine normalization to atoms \(0,t,1\) with masses \(a,b,c\), direct symbolic differentiation of the exact second and fourth central moments gives \(\kappa'(t)=4abc\,t(1-t)((3b-1)t+(3c-1))/V(t)^3\). Hence a nonuniform interior critical point exists exactly when the endpoint masses \(a,c\) lie on the same side of \(1/3\), at \(t_*=(1-3c)/(3b-1)\). Substitution gives \(\kappa_*=(1-3(ab+bc+ca))/(ab+bc+ca-9abc)\). The derivative sign yields the minimum, maximum, and monotone phase cases, while the limits at \(t\downarrow0\) and \(t\uparrow1\) are \(1/(c(1-c))-3\) and \(1/(a(1-a))-3\). For \(a=b=c=1/3\), the kurtosis simplifies identically to \(3/2\). An independent symbolic reconstruction re-derived the derivative factorization, the critical-value identity, and the uniform case.
residual_risks: The centered-vector proportionality statement is read in its nonuniform unique-stationary-point context; the uniform case has a continuum of stationary normalized supports.

value.rationale: For a three-atom distribution with fixed masses, optimizing standardized fourth moment over support geometry is a natural exact invariant. The result gives the complete minimum/maximum/monotone phase diagram, a sharp \(1/3\) transition, the exact stationary support, and the full attainable interval for every mass triple.
residual_risks: The result is restricted to three atoms and one-dimensional Pearson kurtosis.

limitations: Masses are positive and fixed; support points are distinct and considered up to affine normalization.
No claim is made for four or more support points or for alternative kurtosis functionals.
